prose: Cory Doctorow, as once-extinct diseases sweep America - sickening, maiming and killing - finds anti-vax superstition ever harder to excuse, and links it to the broader war on institutional memory: his subtitle is 'remembering saves lives'.

The edition's link roundup includes the Copyright Office and regulatory capture, open licenses vs uncopyrightable subjects, EU link policy, RIP Gutenberg founder Michael Hart, and Wells Fargo's massive fraud.
highlights: Doctorow: anti-vax belief is increasingly inexcusable as extinct diseases return
His through-line: 'remembering saves lives' - memory as public health
Roundup: Copyright Office capture, open licenses, EU link policy
Also: RIP Project Gutenberg founder Michael Hart, Wells Fargo fraud
